audio_caption: The clip begins with a male speaker starting a tutorial, introducing the topic of linking a Samsung smart TV with Alexa in the updated SmartThings app, encouraging the audience to "stick around." The speaker recalls having "pretty limited control," and then explains that Samsung has updated the SmartThings app, which has given the user "a bit more control." The clip ends with the speaker encouraging the listener to remove the Alexa skill and unlink the accounts.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker recommending connecting a TV to a wireless network rather than a wired one. He justifies this by explaining that with wireless, the connection stays active, and on-commands can be used to turn the TV on, whereas a wired Ethernet port turns off and no longer responds. The speaker speaks in a calm, informative tone.

The clip begins with a male speaker instructing the listener to verify that the SmartThings app is up to date. He notes they are using version 1.7.54.21 and to make sure the app is updated and using SmartThings, not SmartThings Classic. He adds that you may need to go through and set up a SmartThings account, and goes on to note that he already has, and that it will take you to the home screen.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker explaining how to add a device, stating to "tap on the little plus sign right here," followed by choosing the device. He suggests using a QR code to scan, adding that "both of those options, at least for me, didn't work very well," so he'll choose the item from the list, tapping "TV" and then "Samsung," noting that there is a chance of "regional lock out" if the device isn't found. He adds there's a button for "supported devices" for more information, and states he'll tap on TV. The speaker mentions the process, saying, "Getting things ready, let's get started with your TV." He states he'll "tap start" for the location, leaving it as default to "my home master." Choosing "living room," he explains to tap "next" after selecting a room. He mentions to "turn on your TV," stating to wait for the device to talk to each other to see if they'll get a pin code.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker describing how the TV challenger device has been found on the network. He states that you may need to connect to your TV, and then to check the pin shown on your TV and enter it below. He then punches in the pin code into the TV and taps done. Next, he mentions that the TV is being registered to your Samsung account. The clip concludes with him adding the device into the SmartThings app.

A male speaker explains that the next step is to link SmartThings with the Alexa app using the SmartThings skill in Alexa. He advises listeners to download the Alexa app if they haven't already done so, mentioning the Play Store and App Store. The speaker has a casual and informative tone.

The clip starts with someone speaking, suggesting to navigate to the Alexa app and tap on either "Browse Skills" or "More" to access skills and games. The speaker then explains to click on the magnifying glass to search for "SmartThings," advising to choose "SmartThings" and not "SmartThings Classic." The tone is instructional and clear. One male speaker is heard.

The audio begins with a male speaker explaining that "account linking is required." His tone is informative and instructional. He then tells the listener to "tap on where it says enable to use" and that it will bring a prompt to "sign in with the Samsung account." He emphasizes the need to use the same account to sync the devices. He reiterates to "sign in with Samsung account," and that one needs to punch in that information once it loads.

The audio clip begins with a single male speaker, instructing the listener to click "authorize" in the SmartThings app to allow Amazon Alexa access. He explains that this will sync locations, devices, and scenes between the two apps. He continues in a casual, instructional tone, stating that the SmartThings account has been successfully linked.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker instructing the listener to close a window to discover smart home devices, and then clicks the "close" option. The same speaker explains that a window will appear, offering the option to "discover devices," potentially taking up to 45 seconds. He suggests that if the device isn't found, the listener should "delink everything, remove everything" and try the setup process again. The speaker then indicates they'll wait to see if the living room TV can be found.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker with an enthusiastic tone, stating "perfect, so she did find the TV". He says "one TV found and connected", and then "Your TV has been added to your Alexa account". He concludes with "next continue setting up your device". This is followed by silence.

A male speaker begins by discussing the capability to control and organize a device like any other smart device. He then walks through the process of device setup, including adding a TV to a group, then skipping that step. He states that the "living room TV is set up and ready to use" and then he recommends one say "so and so turn on the living room TV," after which he clicks done. The speaker then notes the user can "give it a try" and the male speaker initiates several voice commands, one after another, saying "Alexa, turn off living room TV," followed by "Alexa, turn on living room TV," then "Alexa, set volume to 40 on living room TV," and finally "Alexa, change to HDMI one." The speaker then observes that, "as you can see, I have a little bit more control on what I can do."

A male speaker describes how the updated SmartThings app now allows control over a TV's volume, inputs, and channels. He mentions that he still can't launch the apps, which he believes is a feature for newer models. The tone is informative and conversational. He states that he will include a link with a list of supported models and the level of integrations. He concludes that the linking process between the two systems is smooth and streamlined.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker wrapping up a tutorial, expressing gratitude to the viewers, encouraging them to like, share, and subscribe, and directing them to the Helpcloud website for merchandise. He concludes with "Peace." This is followed by upbeat hip-hop music with a positive and energetic vibe.
